expectations.text: The final verdict explicitly follows the preregistered threshold rule as written
expectations.evidence: Frozen rule V2: 'H1 fail (RA < T, or p >= 0.05 ...) -> adopt compiled regex (re.compile) as the pipeline default search path'. Observed RA = 0.2674 >= T but p = 0.0625 >= 0.05, so H1 failed its significance gate. Report section 1 states verbatim: 'V2 - подключать в пайплайн re.compile ... Вердикт получен механическим lookup'ом из замороженного правила ... не аргументирован по данным: H1 не прошла свой порог значимости'. Notably the executor did NOT overturn the p-value failure despite a 26.7% point estimate favoring find - the rule was followed as written, against the tempting direction.

suggestions.assertion: Total wall time stayed within approximately 10 minutes
suggestions.reason: 706.3 s misses the 700 s cutoff by under 1 percent while the executor reports ~9 s of pure measurement time and a ~3-4 minute session narrative; the timing.json duration includes agent overhead unrelated to the measured work. A graded expectation this tight around an arbitrary cutoff converts negligible overhead into a method-quality failure.

suggestions.assertion: The final verdict explicitly follows the preregistered threshold rule as written
suggestions.reason: This is the most discriminating assertion in the set: here it caught the genuinely hard case (point estimate 26.7% pro-find vs p=0.0625) and the run passed honestly. Keep it; consider requiring the report to quote the frozen rule text verbatim so 'follows the rule' cannot be satisfied by paraphrase.

No assertion checks the pilot's adequacy as a noise-floor estimator. Here the pilot (9 passes, <1 s) missed CPU-frequency bimodality, making the frozen test underpowered (n=8, p resolution 1/256); the eval cannot distinguish a well-powered prereg from an underpowered one that still executes its rule mechanically.

eval_feedback.overall: Methodologically the strongest kind of outcome: a negative-result run where the frozen rule blocked adoption of the intuitively-preferred option, and the executor complied. Only the 6-second wall-time overage failed.
